_comment: FRONTIER point: 1 stages x 16 loops = 16 block-steps/token.
The stages<->width tradeoff at FIXED parameters and FIXED compute. Every
point here is 492,418 parameters (this one 492,449, +0.01%) and 16 block-steps/token.
Only n_stages, max_loops, and the width that split forces differ. This is a
frontier rather than two arms: the compute-matched pair already answered
the two-endpoint question (width wins 2:1 at matched params AND compute),
and this traces the whole curve to show whether reuse wins anywhere in the
interior.
Config from examples/param_match.rs with a pinned target:
cargo run --example param_match -- 16 1 492418
KNOWN LIMITATION, recorded before running: width does not fall
monotonically as stages rise (d_model 176 -> 128 -> 64 -> 64 -> 80). The
solver takes the smallest d_model that still reaches the target with a
legal ffn_hidden, so at high stage counts ffn_hidden collapses instead
(512 -> 213 -> 10). Stages is therefore confounded with how much of each
stage's budget goes to attention versus FFN. The three interior points
(s02/s04/s08) keep ffn substantial and are the interpretable subset.
Head count also varies (11 -> 8 -> 4 -> 4 -> 5) and unavoidably so:
trading stages for width at fixed parameters IS trading heads for stages.
That is the axis under test, not a nuisance.
Rung: same-rule (subst-fst-fixed, k_set [0], k0_rate 1.0). This rung
rewards parameters-as-storage and is indifferent to
parameters-as-compute, so a win here would NOT establish that reuse buys
computation. A negative result IS informative about the reuse premise.
Run:
cargo run --example scaling_sweep -- \
research/experiments/frontier-s01l16.json depth gpu 16 \
